epics.description: Customers can export their paid orders as a CSV file from their account page. The export contains one row per paid order with order number, date and total amount including VAT, excludes cancelled orders, and uses the file name pattern orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv. Delimiter and encoding follow the project CSV export convention (UTF-8 without BOM, semicolon-delimited, header row, dates as YYYY-MM-DD, amounts with a dot and two decimals).

features.description: Customer capability to download a CSV file of their paid orders from the account page.
features.name: Order export

acceptanceCriteria: Given I am logged in and on my account page, When I trigger the export action, Then a CSV file is downloaded to my device.
Given the export is triggered on a given day in Europe/Paris, When the file is downloaded, Then its name is orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv with the export date.
Given the file is generated, When I open it, Then it is UTF-8 without BOM, uses a semicolon delimiter and has a header row.
stories.aiReadyReason: The story defines the export action, the file name pattern orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv using the Europe/Paris export date, and the UTF-8 without BOM, semicolon-delimited, header-row format fixed by the project CSV convention, so a developer can implement and verify it; row content is delegated to s2.
stories.description: An export action on the customer account page downloads a CSV file. The file name follows orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv, where the date is the export date in Europe/Paris. The file is UTF-8 without BOM, semicolon-delimited, with a header row, as defined by the project CSV export convention. Content rules are covered by the dependent story.
stories.iWant: to download my paid orders as a CSV file from my account page
stories.soThat: I can keep a record of my purchases

tasks.description: Backend action that returns a CSV file to the logged-in customer only, with Content-Disposition naming the file orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv, where the date is the current date in Europe/Paris. The response is UTF-8 without BOM, uses a semicolon delimiter and starts with a header row, following the project CSV export convention. Expected result: an authenticated request returns the file with the correct name and format, and an unauthenticated request is rejected.
tasks.title: Implement authenticated CSV download endpoint with Europe/Paris file name

tasks.description: Frontend export action on the account page that triggers the CSV download from the backend endpoint and saves the file to the user's device. Expected result: when logged in and on the account page, triggering the action downloads the CSV file.
tasks.title: Add export action on the customer account page

tasks.description: Automated tests covering the three acceptance criteria: download triggered from the account page, file name orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv using the Europe/Paris export date (including a case near midnight Paris time), and file encoding (UTF-8 without BOM), semicolon delimiter and header row. Expected result: all tests pass and verify the acceptance criteria.
tasks.title: Write tests for the CSV export download acceptance criteria

stories.title: Download paid orders CSV from account page

acceptanceCriteria: Given I have several paid orders, When I export my orders, Then the file contains exactly one data row per paid order with its order number, date and total amount including VAT.
Given I have a cancelled order, When I export my orders, Then that order does not appear in the file.
Given an exported order date and total, When the file is generated, Then the date is formatted YYYY-MM-DD and the amount uses a dot and two decimals.
stories.aiReadyReason: The story explicitly leaves undefined which date the date column holds (order placement, payment capture or delivery), a business rule that changes the exported data; should the date column contain the order placement date, the payment capture date, or the delivery date?
dependencies: Download paid orders CSV from account page
stories.description: The CSV contains one row per paid order with three data columns: order number, date and total amount including VAT. A paid order is an order whose payment is captured and which is not fully refunded; cancelled orders are never paid and are excluded. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD and amounts use a dot and two decimals. The specification does not state which date the date column holds (order placement, payment capture or delivery), and this decision is missing.
stories.iWant: the exported file to list each of my paid orders with its order number, date and total amount including VAT, excluding cancelled orders
stories.soThat: I have an accurate summary of my paid purchases
stories.title: Export one row per paid order with order number, date and VAT-inclusive total
